(i) the one machine problem is solvable in O(n) and the parallel machine problem is solvabe in O(n log m) time; (ii) both problems can be encoded in a polynomial size integer program; and (iii) the parallel machine problem with a fixed number m of machines is solvable in polynomial-time if the number K of job-classes is fixed.
(a) the one machine problem can be solved in linear time, and (b) the parallel machine problem can be solved in linear time if the number of job-class is fixed.

the one machine scheduling with arbitrary processing times problem and the parallel machines with identical processing times problem are solvable in time O(n) and O(nlogn) respectively, when the number of job classes is fixed.

the development of polynomial time algorithms for the one machine scheduling and parallel machine scheduling problems with fixed number of job classes.
the development of low-complexity algorithms which are capable to solve scheduling problems with change-over times.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for a fixed number of classes K, the one machine scheduling and parallel machine scheduling problems can be solved in time O(n) and O(n log n), respectively, where n is the number of jobs.
we have shown that the one and the parallel machines problems are solvable by a polynomial time algorithm if the number of job classes is fixed.

for the one machine scheduling with arbitrary processing times the complexity of our algorithms is polynomial in n and log n, while for the parallel machine scheduling problem with identical machine processing times the complexity is polynomial in the number of machines and n and log n.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the one machine and parallel machine scheduling problems, the fixed number of job-class assumption allows us to design polynomial time algorithms that are of low-complexity.
the problem of scheduling jobs with a fixed job-class structure can be solved in polynomial time even if the number of job-class combinations is exponential.
the complexity of scheduling with change-over time can be reduced significantly by fixing the number of job classes.
